KY-2026-SB98.title: AN ACT relating to welding safety.

KY-2026-SB197.title: AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency.
KY-2026-SB197.summary: Create a new section of Subchapter 32 of KRS Chapter 154 to establish a tiered county system for eligible companies to receive incentives under the Kentucky Business Investment Program; amends KRS 154.32-010 to define "tier"; amends KRS 154.32-020 and 154.32-040 to conform; amend KRS 154.32-050 to specify tiering procedures; amend KRS 154.32-060 to require the Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority to identify and certify or decertify the tiers for all counties on an annual basis into 4 tax credit tiers; provide that the incentives available under this subchapter be determined based on the county where the economic development project is located by an approved company; provide a county's tier will be based on a 5 year average of its unemployment rate and population ranking; amend KRS 154.32-090, 154.61-010, 154.61-020, and 141.383 to conform.

KY-2026-SB197.aiSummary: The bill sets up a new county tier system for the Kentucky Business Investment Program, which helps approved companies get tax breaks and other incentives. Counties would be placed into four tax credit tiers each year based on unemployment and population data from the last five years. The level of aid for a project would depend on which county it is in. It was enacted as Chapter 202, with some line items vetoed.

KY-2026-SB56.title: AN ACT relating to utilization controls for nonopioid analgesics in the Medicaid program.
KY-2026-SB56.summary: Create a new section of KRS Chapter 205 to prohibit the Department for Medicaid Services, any Medicaid managed care organization contracted by the department, and the Medicaid state pharmacy benefit manager from denying coverage for a nonopioid analgesic in favor of opioid analgesic or establishing more restrictive or more extensive utilization controls for nonopioid analgesics than the least restrictive or extensive utilization controls for any opioid or narcotic analgesic; require the Cabinet for Health and Family Services or the Department for Medicaid to seek federal approval if it is determined that such approval is necessary; provide authorization from the General Assembly to make changes to the Medicaid program as required under KRS 205.5372(1).

KY-2026-SB281.policyArea: Children And Minors, Civil Procedure, Domestic Relations
KY-2026-SB281.aiSummary: The bill would change how courts decide grandparent visitation cases in Kentucky. It would require clear and convincing evidence, which is a higher proof standard, and set factors a court may use to decide the child’s best interests. It would also update another child welfare law to match these changes.
